environment.directories: lab: http://198.18.0.1:8080/; realworld, startup and rw-recheck: http://213.163.75.157:56050/ (temporary, on p2p-relay1); relay step: 127.0.0.1 on the Hetzner machine
environment.paths: As in campaigns 1-3. Lab: every access link 10 ms each way, relay link 10 ms each way (direct RTT ~40 ms, relayed ~80 ms); lossy1 50 ms + 1 % loss each way. Hetzner <-> i3D host: per flow either ~34 ms or ~37.5 ms RTT (the two route clusters of every campaign); lab nodes with uplink=real reach the real relay through the i3D host's hairpin NAT in < 1 ms.
environment.bench_settings: defaults of 5c5396a, otherwise campaign 3's: latency 12 s at 200 ms, 64 B, packet loss counted from when the selected path has been stable for max(1 s, 3 x min RTT) (peer.latency.loss); upload and download 10 MB each, stopped at 8 s (an upload is reset there and the listener reports what arrived; an upload written completely before 8 s is not stopped, and its count is awaited until 8 s or, if later, max(3 s, the upload's duration, 3 smoothed RTTs) after the end of writing, at most 30 s; new: second_half_mbps); concurrency 8 streams of echo requests, 8 MB, 256 KiB each or smaller on a slow link (new: sized for the lowest of the upload's and download's throughput_mbps and second_half_mbps, so that each stream can finish about four in 8 s; if none has finished by 4 s, the requests in flight are cut off and the phase starts over with requests 1/16 the size, at least 4 KiB, concurrency.restart), requests still running at 8 s are cut off; the phase now ends and is timed when its workers finish (was: at the next 200 ms tick); relay transfers capped at 4 MB; relay_fallback_failed only if nothing got through the relay-only connection; timeout 10 s; --compare-relay and --idle 60s where listed. The relay group uses --relay-only on both sides; the parallel relay runs skip the concurrency phase.
environment.method: Same scenarios (scenarios.jsonl identical to campaign 3's), run counts and order as campaigns 1-3 (harness/campaign/campaign4.sh = campaign3.sh with a new name, output directory and comparison, plus the load sampling): every run starts fresh processes (new iroh keys and ports; bench uses a temporary identity); 3 runs per scenario, rounds interleaved; parallel relay runs: 2 rounds of 2 and of 4 benches. Scenario side a = the bench (client, dialer), b = the listen node. Verdicts classified by summarize.py, which judges each campaign by the rules of its own bench (re-run on campaigns 1-3 it reproduces their classification). Extra, not in summary.json: 10 more lab-netem-pr runs (same nodes and arguments, --compare-relay) in debug/lossy-extra (as in campaign 3), for the loss detection rate, the upload count, the request sizing and restarts on the lossy link; and debug/rw-recheck: 9 re-runs of the direct real-world scenarios with the Hetzner listener (rw-easy-to-ufw, rw-symmetric-to-open, rw-easy-to-open without --compare-relay) right after a fresh lab.sh up campaign-real, to check the slow Hetzner -> lab downloads.
environment.sides: a = the node running `golem-p2p bench` (it dials), b = the node running `golem-p2p listen`

observations.title: The upload count race is fixed: no 'closed stream', no transfer_failed in 124 runs
observations.detail: No bench.jsonl of the 111 campaign runs or the 13 lossy-link runs (3 campaign + 10 debug/lossy-extra) contains 'closed stream'; every upload and download succeeded (no error_kind), and no run has a transfer_failed issue. On the lossy link 10 uploads were stopped at 8 s and their counts arrived 8.12-8.15 s after their start, 3 were written completely: two fast ones (10 MB in 2.6 and 3.2 s) and debug/lossy-extra run9, written completely before 8 s but counted only at 11.0 s (7.3 Mbps): the case that failed with 'read error: closed stream' in campaign 3 (lossy-extra run10) now waits past the time limit for the count (limited_by size, ok). Campaign 3: 1 failure in 13 lossy runs.

observations.title: Fast-path concurrency throughput is measured now (no 200 ms quantization)
observations.detail: The phase now ends when its workers do. Lab direct: 185-252 Mbps (33 runs, 33 distinct values, 250-340 ms for 7.5 MiB; campaign 3: 155.7-156.4 Mbps in all 33, 402-404 ms); lab relayed: 74-81 Mbps (386-424 ms; campaign 3 snapped to 74.2 or 78.1); real world direct 213-330 Mbps (191-295 ms) apart from the three slow runs below; real-world relayed 138-208 Mbps; relay-only through p2p-relay1 65-87 Mbps. The parallel requests run at 1.5-2.3x the single 10 MB / 4 MB transfers, which start from a cold congestion window while the concurrency phase runs on the one the transfers opened. The compare flags 'concurrency 156 -> 190-241 Mbps' in 10 lab scenarios and on rw-easy-to-open / rw-open-to-symmetric are this fix, not a speed-up.

observations.title: Lossy link: loss detected in 9 of 13 runs (sampling), the count always settled
observations.detail: lab-netem-pr (1 % loss each way): packet_loss hint in 2 of 3 campaign runs and 7 of 10 extra runs, 9/13 (campaign 3: 11/13). latency.loss was never null: counting started 1.14-1.32 s into the phase, windows of 114-121 packets, 1-3 lost where detected. The four misses lost 0 of 117-118 packets; at 1 % random loss 0.99^117 = 31 % of such windows show no loss, so ~4 misses in 13 runs is the expected rate (campaigns 3+4: 6 misses in 26 runs, 23 %). No miss was at or above the threshold (no 'wrong' check).

observations.title: Lossy link: concurrency throughput in 13 of 13 runs; 2 restarts
observations.detail: The second-half rule lowered the request sizing in 11 of 13 runs (by 1.1-3.5x against campaign 3's slower-average rule: e.g. 4.02 -> 1.26, 3.30 -> 0.94, 8.00 -> 4.32, 5.51 -> 2.08 Mbps); requests were sized for 0.70-4.32 Mbps (21-131 KiB) and every run measured 0.46-3.64 Mbps (median 0.95; campaign 3: 11/13). In the 11 runs without a restart the size was within 0.3-2.0x of what the phase then measured. Restarts: debug/lossy-extra run8 (sized for 4.32 Mbps from the upload's second half, 131 KiB; none of the 8 had finished at 4.0 s; started over with 8 KiB, 28 finished, 0.46 Mbps) and run9 (sized for 2.08 Mbps from the download's second half, 63 KiB; restarted at 4.0 s with 4 KiB, 139 finished, 1.14 Mbps). Run8 needed it (its 1.07 MB of first requests reached the listener only after 9.6 s). Run9's link was over-estimated only ~2x (download second half 2.08 Mbps, the echoes then came back at ~1 Mbps): its 8 requests had reached the listener within 1 s and ~80 % of their echoes (412 of 516 KB) were back when the restart cut them off at 4.0 s, so they would have finished shortly after; sized for four requests per stream in 8 s, a ~2x over-estimate in the slower direction puts the first replies at about the 4 s restart point. In the 11 runs without a restart the fastest requests took 0.16-2.0 s. No restart in the 90 clean-link peer runs (fast paths finish their first request in milliseconds).

observations.title: New bug: cut-off concurrency requests are not cancelled on the wire
observations.detail: Requests cut off by a restart or by the 8 s limit keep sending. Endpoint::request_from (crates/golem-p2p/src/endpoint.rs) resets the stream when its future is dropped only while `complete` is false, i.e. before write_all + finish returned; write_all returns as soon as the payload is in the stream's send buffer, which for requests up to the stream window (1.25 MB) is at once, so the workers' dropped futures leave fully buffered requests that QUIC still delivers (and retransmits). Seen in the listener logs: debug/lossy-extra run8's 8 cut-off 134,144-byte requests reached the listener 5.6-5.8 s after the restart (1.6-1.8 s after the phase ended): of the 1.17 MB the bench sent in the 8 s phase only 0.23 MB were the counted 8 KiB requests, the rest mostly the cut-off 131 KiB requests, so the restart's 0.46 Mbps understates a link that carried ~1.2 Mbps up in that phase. In 7 of 13 lossy runs requests cut off at the time limit still arrived at the listener after the phase had ended (up to 3.9 s later, debug/lossy-extra run7 with 105 KiB requests), i.e. during relay_compare's latency measurement on the same access link. (The listener's echoes stop: the dropped RecvStream sends STOP_SENDING.) Fix: reset the send stream on drop unless the response was read (track completion of the whole exchange, not just of the write); request_from's own timeout path already resets after finish.

observations.title: Slow Hetzner -> lab direction in 3 real-world runs (environment; seen in campaigns 1 and 3 too)
observations.detail: rw-easy-to-ufw runs 1-2 and rw-symmetric-to-open run 1 (01:34:00-01:36:20 UTC, lab bench, Hetzner listener, direct) downloaded at 13.7-15.6 Mbps (second half 20-22 Mbps) while uploads in the same runs ran at 132-144 Mbps; their concurrency took 2.8-4.3 s (14.6-22.4 Mbps, request RTT ~0.7-1 s) while the small loaded-RTT probes stayed at 37-46 ms (no queue building up), and the bench counted no loss (it counts only its own packets). Relayed runs in the same minutes (Hetzner -> relay over TCP) ran at 73-85 Mbps, and rw-easy-to-open run 1 at 01:34:56 at 146 Mbps. This machine's load average was 36-45 then (24-49 over the step, other sessions). Not reproduced: 9 re-runs right after a fresh lab.sh up campaign-real at 01:57-02:00 (debug/rw-recheck, load 23-24) all ran at 131-148 Mbps both ways (concurrency 235-313 Mbps). The same symptom hit 1 run in campaign 1 (rw-symmetric-to-open run 3, 14.5 Mbps) and 2 in campaign 3 (8.8 and 13.8 Mbps), with older code; the listener's sending side is unchanged since campaign 3 and the bench's download now only records progress, so this is the environment (the internet path toward the i3D host, or CPU contention on this machine), not a regression. The verdicts report the measured numbers.

observations.title: Outcomes, RTT and throughput unchanged otherwise
observations.detail: All 35 scenarios keep their direct/relay outcome; final paths 51 direct / 42 relay / 0 failed in the 93 peer runs, no connection lost, QUIC counters in all 93 (as in campaigns 2-3). Issue, hint, status and exit-code counts are identical to campaign 3 in every scenario. Lab RTT (40.4 ms direct, 80.6 ms relayed), throughput (122-124 / 35-36 Mbps), bind and connect times match campaign 3 within noise. Real-world RTT and throughput moved with the two route clusters (~34 / ~37.5 ms). Benches on this machine bound 50-60 ms slower (load, see build_machine_load). Clean-link peer runs are ~0.1 s shorter (the concurrency phase ends with its workers); lossy runs 60.6-72.7 s (campaign 3: 58-70.5 s), extra runs 63.0-74.0 s.

observations.title: Verdicts: 110 runs right, 1 misleading, 0 wrong (as in campaign 3)
observations.detail: Checks 254 / 1 / 0. The misleading run is lab-netem-pr run 1: 1 % loss on the link, but 0 of the 118 packets in the settled window were lost, so no packet_loss hint (sampling, as campaign 3's run 3). No false positives: 0 of 11,335 settled latency-phase packets lost in the 90 clean-link peer runs, no packet_loss hint on any of them. Not counted (debug runs): 3 more sampling misses among the 10 extra lossy runs; no misleading transfer_failed any more.

observations.title: The real relay is not a bottleneck at the tested load (unchanged)
observations.detail: Relay-only Hetzner -> p2p-relay1 -> Hetzner: 37-41 Mbps per 4 MB transfer alone, ~40.5 Mbps each with 2 and with 4 at once (160-163 Mbps aggregate), no packets dropped by the relay; 418.3 MB through the relay in total, as in campaigns 1-3.

limitations: 3 runs per scenario (4-8 for the parallel relay runs): percentiles over runs are rough; RTT percentiles pool the ~60 latency samples of each run. The lossy-link medians say little; its detection rate and restart counts come from 13 runs (3 campaign runs + 10 extra in debug/lossy-extra, which are not in summary.json).

The verdict classification is ours (summarize.py), per run by its worst finding; a 'right' run can still have imperfect wording. A packet_loss hint on an unshaped path counts as misleading, also in the real world where one lost packet may be real. A transfer_failed issue is not checked against what the listener received (none occurred).
The packet_loss window holds 112-145 packets: at 1 % random loss about one window in three shows no loss, so a single run cannot tell 1 % loss from none.

The build machine was shared with other sessions (load average 24-49 on 32 vCPU during the steps that run there, hetzner-load.txt); bind times there are ~50-60 ms higher than in campaign 3, and CPU contention cannot be ruled out for the three slow Hetzner -> lab downloads.

The lab NATs are Linux conntrack + nftables with port preservation, one host per router, silent drops of unsolicited packets and one mapping timeout; the 'inbound packet steals the port' behaviour of the i3D host's NAT is not reproduced, and a NAT reboot keeps the same ports.
One relay per scenario: mapping_varies_by_dest cannot be measured, so hard_nat (two relays) was never exercised; hard_nat_likely (one relay, port not preserved) was.

No rate limits in the lab and fixed transfer sizes (10 MB direct, 4 MB relayed): throughput numbers show slow start for those sizes, not capacity; the concurrency phase runs on the congestion window the transfers opened and is 1.5-2.3x faster on fast paths.
Real world: one location (Helsinki) and one firewall type (ufw); per-flow routes of ~34 or ~37.5 ms between the i3D host and Hetzner shift RTT and throughput by ~8 % between runs and campaigns.

Concurrency requests cut off by a restart or the time limit keep sending (bug above), so after a restart the counted throughput can understate the link, and leftovers of the last requests overlap the start of relay_compare on lossy links.
The relay load test is bounded (at most 4 parallel 4 MB transfers, ~150 MB through the relay) and does not find the relay's capacity.
--idle cannot show NAT mapping expiry: iroh keeps every path alive every 5 s and the lab's shortest mapping timeout is 5 s.
QUIC loss is counted only for packets the bench node sent; IPv4 only inside the lab.
Runs were sequential, but the i3D host also carries other services; their load was not controlled.
